Their frequencies and costs must be measured rather than chosen to favor either arm.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"12. Key collision and recovery introduce different risks\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"A separate two-operation regression test is necessary because the primary task requires only one operation. Give two valid grants for distinct operations p1 and p2, sufficient funds, timely receipts, and settlement. With distinct keys both arms have per-operation counts (1,1) and satisfy the two-operation rubric. If the client incorrectly assigns the same K to both, B still obtains (1,1), whereas correct A obtains (1,0): p2 is rejected as KEY_CONFLICT because operation identity is part of the payload. A's two-operation success is false, but duplicate/unauthorized harm is zero. If payload checking instead omits operation identity and silently returns p1's receipt for p2, that is an additional implementation defect; an oracle checking operation IDs rejects it. Conversely, changing K to escape a conflict after an ambiguous first commitment can create two effects for the first operation. Conflicts therefore require reconciliation or explicit escalation, not automatic new-key retry. Deduplication introduces storage, contention, access-control, retention, and reconciliation obligations; these can shift risk from duplication to omission or availability.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"13. Oracle audit and reproducible next test\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Implement the ledger and an independently written event-replay oracle from this specification. The oracle must compare exact fixture intent, append-only transaction multiplicities, commit-time authorization versions, both sides of each balanced posting, settlement records, queued-request fences, client output timestamps, and budget counters. Final net balances alone are insufficient because compensation or offsetting errors could hide duplicate effects. First test the listed paired schedules, then enumerate bounded interleavings around authorization, atomic persistence, acknowledgment, restart, settlement, expiry, and record retention. Independently check transaction counts against account deltas and deliberately corrupt logs/receipts to verify that missing or inconsistent evidence is not certified as success. Preserve raw events, fixture versions, fault schedules, and arm configuration. Such finite tests would assess implementation fidelity, not prove the general invariant or establish population benefit. Later repeated independent task clusters should report success, total and delayed harm, safe stops, latency, calls, and cost with uncertainty; the previous comparison bound requires separately justified oracle-error allowances.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"c8070adb-7c30-44b1-b0ad-e838053aaf29\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"14. Relation to supplied work and project-level limits\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"The supplied extract of c8070adb-7c30-44b1-b0ad-e838053aaf29 identifies the missing ledger/oracle semantics; this specification advances that duty but does not implement or audit it. Peer extract fdfb1b57-9f8a-451c-b9b4-2cca9cbf618f highlights ambiguous acknowledgments and a durable effect-plus-receipt contract. I adopt those as design questions, independently derive the invariant here, and do not transfer its impossibility bound: its assurance that retries commit is unnecessary for this safety proof and absent from several controls. Peer extract 2c4dca26-4c2f-4c55-bab1-b11bb97a5954 and prior extract 0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8 reinforce that judge agreement cannot validate truth allowances; their truncated formulas and omitted arguments are not premises here. Their originals were not supplied. Operational failure ada09312-ae3f-43ea-a461-b2a04b05f66b is not evidence against the mathematics and is not retried. The contribution is a proposed auditable mechanism specification using standard transaction reasoning. Material novelty relative to literature, real-tool contract compliance, practical overhead, empirical generality, and effects on open-ended agent tasks are not assessed.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"c8070adb-7c30-44b1-b0ad-e838053aaf29\\\",\\n        \\\"fdfb1b57-9f8a-451c-b9b4-2cca9cbf618f\\\",\\n        \\\"2c4dca26-4c2f-4c55-bab1-b11bb97a5954\\\",\\n        \\\"0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8\\\"\\n      ]\\n    }\\n  ],\\n  \\\"claim_is_conditional\\\": true,\\n  \\\"assumptions\\\": [\\n    \\\"All economic effects occur within the specified closed ledger; commitment and durable key/receipt insertion are one serializable atomic transaction, and recovery preserves both or neither.\\\",\\n    \\\"Every retry for one operation uses the same pre-journaled scoped key and exact payload; distinct intended operations receive distinct keys, and retained key bindings cannot disappear while old requests remain admissible.\\\",\\n    \\\"Authentication and commit-time authorization are enforced independently of deduplication; grants bind exact fixture intent, expire at E, and cannot be renewed by the client in this experiment.\\\",\\n    \\\"Settlement marks an existing txid without another economic posting. The core completion contract additionally requires settlement within s and permanent economic closure by H>E+s.\\\",\\n    \\\"The bounded client policy, deadlines, budgets, receipt checks, and stopping rules are fixed in advance. Timeouts do not cancel queued requests.\\\",\\n    \\\"The paired truth-table fixtures use isolated identical snapshots, enough funds for all scheduled baseline commitments, an authoritative event order, and the stated deterministic fault schedules. Rows explicitly marked as contract-breaking or changed-policy controls do not satisfy all core premises.\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"evidence_status\\\": \\\"Conditional analytical invariant proof and manually derived oracle truth table for a proposed finite ledger model. Five omitted findings and twenty omitted historical obligations remain unreviewed.\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"python_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"sage_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"prior_session_failure_attempt_ids\\\": [\\n    \\\"ada09312-ae3f-43ea-a461-b2a04b05f66b\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"human_guidance_reviews\\\": [],\\n  \\\"computational_citations\\\": [],\\n  \\\"continuation_reviews\\\": []\\n}\"},\"sequence_number\":5264}\n\nevent: response.output_item.done\ndata: {\"type\":\"response.output_item.done\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"msg_04055f6239acaf7b016ae6979e1f4487d0818c3cc24d9efa40\",\"type\":\"message\",\"status\":\"completed\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"output_text\",\"annotations\":[],\"logprobs\":[],\"text\":\"{\\n  \\\"claim\\\": \\\"Under the explicit ledger contract below, atomic, durable idempotency prevents more than one committed transfer for the same scoped key, including concurrent retries, acknowledgment loss, and crash recovery. If every attempt for one intended operation uses that key, this gives at-most-one commitment for that operation—not guaranteed completion, correct authorization, timely settlement, or end-to-end task success. The specification and paired oracle truth table below distinguish those properties. This is an analytical specification, not an executed experiment or measured architectural benefit.\\\",\\n  \\\"method\\\": \\\"Specify a small ledger, client retry policy, independent outcome oracle, and deterministic paired fault schedules. Hypothesis for a future experiment: stable-key atomic deduplication reduces duplicate commitments after ambiguous timeouts without unacceptable omission, latency, or cost regressions. The discriminating analytical case is a committed request whose acknowledgment is lost: baseline retries can commit twice, whereas the specified intervention replays one durable receipt. Negative controls include dropped requests, missed receipt deadlines, and unauthorized requests; contract-breaking controls include regenerated keys, early record deletion, and non-atomic effect/record writes. Both arms must use isolated identical snapshots, identical authorization and settlement rules, fixed model/prompt versions and resource ceilings, and the same retry policy; baseline ignores the otherwise identical key field. Safeguard overhead counts against the intervention budget. No runtime is available, so no program or execution is requested. The current action addresses the specification portion of the unresolved ledger/oracle obligation; implementation, audit, inference calibration, and empirical effectiveness remain open.\\\",\\n  \\\"reasoning_steps\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"1. Scope, economic effect, and authorization\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"One task intends one transfer p*=(run, operation, source, recipient, positive integer amount, currency). Integer minor units avoid rounding ambiguity. A trusted fixture issues a grant g binding the principal, exact p*, and commit-valid interval [0,E]. The expected intent comes from this fixture, not from an agent-supplied label. Authorization is checked at the commitment linearization point, including revocation, account ownership, and sufficient funds. A grant permits repeated matching submissions during its interval; it is deliberately not a one-use token. Otherwise a one-use authorization service would itself supply the duplicate-prevention intervention. The fixture permits no grant renewal. Commitment atomically posts balanced debit/credit entries; settlement subsequently marks that same transaction final and never posts another debit. This is a closed ledger, not an unmodeled external payment rail.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"2. Minimal auditable state\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"The state is (balances, grants/revocations, transaction log L, deduplication map D, request queue, response queue, client journal). Each transaction contains a unique txid, exact payload, grant identity/version, authorization result, commit sequence/time, and status COMMITTED or SETTLED. D maps a scoped key K to the complete payload and durable committed receipt. Requests have distinct attempt IDs but share an operation identity. Their lifecycle is SENT -> DROPPED or QUEUED -> REJECTED, REPLAYED, or COMMITTED. Responses separately become DELIVERED, DELAYED, or LOST. Client journal entries record the intended payload/key before sending, attempt counts, observed receipts, and final output. Authoritative server events record validation, commitment, replay/conflict, recovery, and settlement; transport fault events record drops and delays. Economic events and their deduplication records must survive the same crashes. The oracle reads server state and the fault schedule, not merely the client's journal.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"3. Key scope, binding, and lifetime\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Define K=(isolated-run epoch, tenant, authenticated principal, transfer-endpoint version, opaque key). One intended operation receives one key, durably journaled before its first send and reused after every timeout or client restart. Distinct operations require distinct keys. D binds K to exact canonical payload equality, including operation ID and all economic fields; equality is not inferred solely from an unchecked hash. Reuse with a different payload returns KEY_CONFLICT and performs no write. Lookup and receipt replay require current read authorization; possession of a key is not authentication. Records survive restart, failover, and snapshot recovery and have no TTL while the namespace exists. Namespace disposal is allowed only with permanent rejection of its old epochs, including restored replicas. A production retention interval would instead need a justified upper bound on every possible replay and restore path; the agent retry deadline alone is insufficient.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"4. Atomic server transition and its baseline\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"For intervention A, Execute(K,p,g) first authenticates access. In one serializable durable transaction: if D[K] exists with p, return its recorded receipt without an economic write; if it exists with a different payload, reject; otherwise recheck current authorization, commit-valid time, and funds, then atomically append one balanced transaction and insert D[K]=(p,receipt). A crash exposes either both writes or neither. Concurrent requests linearize through this transaction; there is no independently durable 'key reserved, effect unfinished' state. Rejected attempts do not reserve keys or cache negative results. A receipt replay may occur after grant expiry or revocation if read access remains valid, but cannot create a new transfer. Baseline B performs the same fresh authorization and balanced posting for each executed attempt, ignoring D. In both arms acknowledgment generation follows durable commitment; losing an acknowledgment never rolls back commitment. Settlement is an idempotent txid-based status transition held fixed between arms.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"5. Bounded retry, delayed responses, and settlement closure\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Fix an agent deadline D_agent, grant expiry E>D_agent, maximum retries R, timeout/backoff schedule, and total call/time/token/monetary ceilings. At most R+1 write attempts may be sent, all before D_agent; reads and reconciliation also consume prespecified budgets. Timeouts mean UNKNOWN, not FAILED or CANCELED. A delayed original request may execute after a retry or after client stopping. A matching committed receipt delivered before D_agent permits final output; subsequent responses cannot trigger a new operation or reset the retry count. A delayed response alone never changes ledger state. At exhaustion the client outputs UNKNOWN/ESCALATE, not success. Choose settlement horizon H>E+s, where each committed transaction settles within s in the core contract. At H, Q=1 means all run transactions are settled and every queued or future old-grant request is permanently unable to create another economic effect. Commit-time expiry supplies this fence; a client stop does not. Fault tests may violate settlement progress, in which case Q can be zero.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"6. Exact success, harmful-event, and safe-stop predicates\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Let L_H be all run-attributable economic commitments through H, including requests still executing after the client stops. Order them by authoritative commit sequence. A commitment is bad if it differs from fixture intent p*, was unauthorized at commitment, or is the second or later commitment for that one intended operation. A settlement event is bad if it settles a bad commitment or creates any extra economic posting. Let Harm_H indicate any bad commitment or settlement by H, and DelayedHarm_(D_agent,H] indicate any such bad event whose event time is in (D_agent,H]. Thus a correct first commitment after D_agent misses the deadline but is not automatically harm; a duplicate committed before D_agent and settled afterward is delayed harm under this event-based definition. Exact task success Y_H=1 iff: L_H contains exactly one commitment, it equals p* and was authorized, its commit time is at most D_agent, it is settled by H, no bad settlement occurred, Q=1, the client output by D_agent contains its matching txid/payload/committed receipt, and all client budget limits were respected. Otherwise Y_H=0. A safe omission stop requires an UNKNOWN/ESCALATE output, L_H empty, Q=1, and no harmful event; it is not task success. Missing audit data produce UNKNOWN labels, not invented zero harm or known success. These are horizon-specific predicates, not claims of lifetime safety.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"7. Proof of the duplicate-commit exclusion\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Initially fix any K with D[K] absent. Induct over serialized server transitions. A rejection, replay, response event, or settlement creates no commitment. The first successful fresh execution inserts exactly one commitment and D[K] together. Thereafter every matching execution takes the replay branch and every mismatching execution takes the conflict branch. Crash recovery preserves both the commitment and D[K], so it cannot restore the absent-key state while retaining the effect. Therefore the commitment count for K is at most one for every finite history. Serialization handles simultaneous attempts; transport order and lost acknowledgments are irrelevant to this invariant. If K is initially occupied, no fresh commitment is possible under it. If every attempt for one operation uses the same K, that operation inherits the bound. A stable operation label without stable K does not establish the premise.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"8. What the invariant does not prove\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Zero commitments satisfies at-most-one. All requests can be dropped, authorization can expire, funds can be insufficient, a receipt can arrive too late, or settlement can fail. Conditional completion additionally follows only if an authorized matching execution linearizes before D_agent, its receipt is delivered and correctly output before D_agent within budget, settlement and closure hold by H, and no other faulty path changes the ledger. Then the invariant supplies uniqueness and these additional conditions supply every remaining clause of Y_H. This is not an eventual-delivery guarantee under bounded retries. Wrong fixture intent, a compromised authorizer, a separate non-deduplicated downstream effect, and writes under fresh keys remain outside the invariant. Atomic idempotency also does not undo a first incorrect authorized transfer.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"9. Accounts contain enough funds for both baseline attempts. Ordinary commitments occur at 1 or 5, settle one unit later, and delivered receipts arrive before 10 unless specified. Both arms receive the same attempt-indexed fault schedule and isolated initial state. A replay produces no settlement event because it creates no transaction. The tuple is (n_D,n_H,r,q,y,d): commitment counts by 10 and 15, whether a matching receipt was output by 10, closure Q, success Y_H, and DelayedHarm_(10,15]. A valid local receipt does not certify uniqueness: r may be 1 when y is 0. All entries are deductions from specified traces, not observations. The table is a set of discriminating witnesses, not exhaustive state-space verification.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"10. Key collision and recovery introduce different risks\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"A separate two-operation regression test is necessary because the primary task requires only one operation. Give two valid grants for distinct operations p1 and p2, sufficient funds, timely receipts, and settlement. With distinct keys both arms have per-operation counts (1,1) and satisfy the two-operation rubric.
